podcast.body: Inspired by Jerry Butler's "For Your Precious Love," this slow-burn ballad was initially rejected by Sid Nathan at Federal Records, who threatened to drop Brown. Convinced it would be a hit, Brown recorded a demo with his own money and took it directly to radio stations, where it quickly became the most requested song. After Federal received orders for 25,000 copies, Nathan reluctantly agreed to properly record the song in a studio at the label's expense. "Try Me" became an even bigger hit than "Please Please Please," reaching number one on the R&B charts and number 48 on the pop charts. "Primee became an even bigger hit than please please please had and went to number one and the R&B charts and number 48 on the pop charts."
